transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-06-05
Time: 15:00 PT
Duration: 45 minutes
Attendees: Evan Martinez (Redwood AE); Priya Rao (Redwood SE); Maya Chen (Skyline Head of ML); Carlos Ruiz (Platform Eng); Lena Novak (CTO)

Summary (auto): quick discovery on model selection, context length, multilingual needs, and tool-calling. Action items captured.

Transcript:
00:00 Evan: Hey everyone, thanks for making time. I'm Evan from Redwood, AE for your account. With me is Priya our solutions engineer. How's everything over on the Skyline side?
00:08 Maya: Hi Evan, thanks. Yep excited to talk through model options. We're evaluating hosted vs dedicated — and potentially private — mainly for a customer-facing agent that needs to be multilingual and do tool calls into our billing / crm systems.
00:20 Evan: Great. High level, we typically ask about scale and throughput, latency targets, context-length needs, and any compliance constraints.
00:26 Carlos: For throughput, it's modest to start — about 30 concurrent sessions at peak, maybe 200k tokens/day, but we expect growth. Latency — we'd like sub 300ms for short queries, - for the simple stuff. For tool-calls, the flow is critical; if the model makes the wrong API call that's bad.
00:45 Priya: Cool. When you say tool-calls, do you mean function-calling / tool invocation with structured args? Or do you mean external retrieval + call orchestration?
00:52 Maya: Both. Primarily function-calling with strict schemas, sometimes with external retrieval first. Also we need Spanish and Portuguese and Chinese coverage.
01:02 Priya: Understood. Quick note on models: the open-model landscape we usually compare is Mistral (lighter / fast), Falcon (strong long-context variants), Llama-family (broad ecosystem), and some newer mosaic / gemma variants. Each has tradeoffs for latency, quantization and tool-calling reliability.
01:20 Lena: Are you able to run function-calling reliably on hosted? We've had issues with hallucinated arguments on other providers.
01:26 Evan: Yes — Redwood supports structured function-calling. We also offerToolkit-level validation where we run schema checks and rerank generations to prefer valid calls. That reduces bad calls dramatically, though nothing is perfect.
01:39 Carlos: What about context length. We're debating 8k vs 32k. Some of our flows require long transcripts — up to 25k tokens on occasion.
01:48 Priya: If you need 25k sometimes, a 32k context model is safer. That said, long context increases compute and latency — so we typically recommend a hybrid: use prefix/KV caching and retrieval-augmented prompts for older context, and reserve 32k models for flows that truly need full history. We can prototype both.
02:10 Maya: Cost-wise, what's the tradeoff?
02:12 Priya: Roughly speaking, 32k models cost 2–4x per token vs 8k for the same model family due to longer attention and memory. But with batching and KV cache you can lower per-token. We'll run bench to show concrete numbers for your traffic pattern.
02:27 Evan: Also consider dedicated vs hosted: hosted is lowest friction, usage-based. Dedicated gives you reserved GPU pools for predictable throughput and can lower unit costs at scale. Private (VPC/on-prem) is an option if you need isolated control plane or strict residency.
02:40 Lena: We do have some regulatory customers in EU, so data residency and KMS integration matter.
02:45 Evan: Absolutely — Redwood Private supports customer-managed VPC and KMS/HSM integrations, audit logs, SOC2 and ISO. We'll share the security pack.
02:54 Carlos: You mentioned quantization — does that affect tool-calling reliability? We've seen some models degrade when heavily quantized.
03:01 Priya: Good question. Quantization can slightly reduce accuracy, especially for subtle formatting tasks, but modern quantization profiles (int8, etc.) maintain decent structure. For function-calling we recommend testing on quantized variants — if you need near-perfect structured outputs, we can keep key paths on fp16. We'll include that in the bench matrix.
03:22 Maya: Any specific model recommendations for multilingual + tool-calling?
03:26 Priya: For multilingual and tool reliability, we often recommend starting with a mid-sized Mistral-family or a Falcon-40B long-context variant. Llama-family has great ecosystem support if you want more fine-tuning. If you need the cheapest path, a quantized Mistral-8x can be very cost-effective.
03:44 Evan: We'll put those recommendations into a simple matrix: accuracy, latency, cost, long-context support, multilingual strength, and function-calling reliability.
03:53 Carlos: Benchmarks — can you run on our prompts?
03:56 Priya: Yes please share a prompt set — ideally 50 sample interactions across languages and tool-call scenarios. We'll run latency/cost/valid-call rate tests.
04:06 Maya: We'll pull that together. One question — how does Redwood's KV cache help?
04:10 Priya: KV cache (prefix caching) stores key/value states for recent tokens, which speeds up generation for repeated contexts and reduces end-to-end latencies on incremental tokens. For chat you can see big wins; for single-shot long prompts it helps less. Also automatic batching improves throughput for many concurrent short requests.
04:27 Lena: If we run a dedicated pilot, what's the timeline?
04:30 Evan: We can do a 2-week dedicated pilot once contracts are in place. Provisioning usually takes 3–5 business days for dedicated pools. For Private (VPC) it's longer — a couple of weeks for networking and KMS onboarding.
04:44 Carlos: Anything we should be careful about during pilot? We need observability per-token costs.
04:49 Evan: Redwood Console provides token-level cost and latency breakdowns, per-route dashboards, and tracing. We'll include the dashboard access during the pilot.
04:59 Maya: Ok good. Also we'll need SOC2 + ISO docs for our procurement.
05:03 Evan: Will send security pack. Also we'll follow up with a schedule for the security review.
05:08 Lena: One more — do you have a recommended fallback plan if the chosen model hits a regression in quality?
05:12 Priya: Yes, Redwood supports rollout policies and automatic fallback to different model variants or older pinned versions if we detect regressions. We also support canary deploys and A/B testing with automatic rollback triggers tied to quality metrics.
05:25 Maya: Perfect.
05:28 Evan: To recap — action items: Evan will send model matrix + pricing and SOC2 docs; Priya runs bench on 8k vs 32k for Mistral and Falcon variants; Maya shares prompt set; schedule security review. Planning a follow-up in ~2 weeks to review bench results and finalize pilot config.
05:45 Evan: Thanks all — we'll follow up over email.
